Road alerts from the map data
Flock and other ALPR cameras mapped in OpenStreetMap. Checked on the phone; nothing about your drive is sent.

Southbound keeps maps, search, routing and voice on your phone. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), shown with the OpenMapTiles schema (© OpenMapTiles). Routing by Valhalla; navigation by Ferrostar (Stadia Maps); map rendering by MapLibre. Built-in voice: Piper \"Amy\" (Mycroft mimic3-voices) run by sherpa-onnx. Extra places in search: © Overture Maps Foundation (overturemaps.org), CDLA Permissive 2.0, kept apart from the OpenStreetMap data. They include data from Foursquare Labs, Inc. under the Apache License 2.0 (Copyright 2024 Foursquare Labs, Inc. All rights reserved.) and from AllThePlaces under CC0.
Everything above works offline. These extras go online only when turned on, and fetch whole feeds, so nothing sent says where you are, what you searched or where you\'re going.
Arrival times and service alerts from MTA. No key needed.
Needs a free key from bustime.mta.info. Stored encrypted on this phone.
Bus Time key saved (type to replace)

Crashes, closures and work zones across the state, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the feeds 511ny.org\'s own map reads.

PennDOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Pennsylvania, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists 511pa.com\'s own map and list pages read.

CTDOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Connecticut, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists ctroads.org\'s own map and list pages read.

MDOT SHA\'s crashes, closures and other events across Maryland, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras (a frame of the live video when you open one) and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the files CHART\'s own traffic map reads.

DelDOT\'s road closures, roadwork and travel alerts across Delaware, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras (a frame of the live video when you open one) and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the files DelDOT\'s own traffic map reads.

WisDOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Wisconsin, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists 511wi.gov\'s own map and list pages read.

IDOT\'s and the Tollway\'s crashes, roadwork and lane closures across Illinois, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows their traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the feeds Travel Midwest\'s own map reads.

NDDOT\'s road alerts and work zones across North Dakota, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras on the map (no message signs). No key needed: these are the map layers NDDOT\'s own travel map reads.

SDDOT\'s road work, restrictions, incidents and closures across South Dakota, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras on the map (no message signs). No key needed: these are the files SD511\'s own map reads.

INDOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Indiana, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists and map query 511in.org\'s own map reads.

MnDOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Minnesota, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists and map query 511mn.org\'s own map reads.

Iowa DOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Iowa, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists and map query 511ia.org\'s own map reads.

Nebraska DOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Nebraska, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists and map query 511.nebraska.gov\'s own map reads.

KDOT\'s crashes, closures and roadwork across Kansas, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the lists and map query kandrive.gov\'s own map reads.

MDOT\'s crashes, closures and work zones across Michigan, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras on the map (a camera\'s picture is fetched when you open it; message signs are not read, their text is one page per sign). No key needed: these are the lists Mi Drive\'s own map reads.

ODOT\'s crashes, closures and construction across Ohio, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. Needs a free OHGO key: register at publicapi.ohgo.com, paste the key below. The key is stored encrypted and sent only to publicapi.ohgo.com.

VDOT\'s crashes, closures, work zones and weather closures across Virginia, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the map layers 511 Virginia\'s own map reads.

WVDOH\'s incidents, closures and roadwork across West Virginia, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras (a frame of the camera\'s live video, fetched when you open it) and message signs on the map. No key needed: these are the files WV511\'s own map reads.

KYTC\'s crashes, closures and work zones across Kentucky, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Also shows its traffic cameras on the map (no message signs: KYTC\'s sign layer hasn\'t changed since 2025). No key needed: these are the map layers KYTC\'s own GoKY map reads.
Turned on by an older backup. Southbound has no TomTom layer: turn it off.
A 511NY key is saved, from before 511NY stopped needing one.
Speeds on NYC highways and main roads from NYC Open Data, fetched whole. No key needed. The city\'s copy sometimes lags; readings older than two hours are not shown.
With any of these on, a traffic button appears on the map. Feeds are fetched only while the layer is shown or while navigating.
Version %1$s is ready. Confirm the install when Android asks, or tap the update notification. Check now asks again.

The map, search and directions for the regions below (main roads come for every state), and NYC transit data, from Southbound\'s GitHub releases, checked daily. Only the files that changed are downloaded, and each is checked against its published SHA-256.
New versions of Southbound from the same releases, checked to be signed with the same key. Android asks you to confirm every one before it installs.
Off: downloads wait for Wi-Fi. Check now always downloads straight away.

Optional. The repository is public, so updates need no token; one only lifts GitHub\'s limit of 60 requests an hour from your address. If an old token stops working, remove it. A token is stored encrypted on this phone and sent only to api.github.com.
Queued: Android starts it once there\'s a connection (Wi-Fi, unless mobile data is allowed). If this stays for more than a minute, close and reopen Southbound.

Tick the regions you want: each brings its map, search and local streets for directions, and main roads in every state come with any of them, so a trip passes through regions you haven\'t ticked. The place you\'re going needs its region: directions to one you haven\'t ticked offer to get it for that trip. Transit schedules cover NYC. Unticking a region deletes its map, search and streets from the phone.
Not downloaded yet; comes with the next update check.
Got for a trip: removed once you\'re back in your own regions.
Night mode by sunset while navigating
After sunset at your location the map and navigation screen turn dark, even if the phone is in light theme. Worked out on the phone from your GPS fix.
Search, Home, Work and the map\'s banners sit at the bottom of the screen, within your thumb\'s reach. Off puts them at the top.
Used to estimate what each route costs in gas.
Gas prices (EIA) is on, but no EIA key is saved. Add one under Live data. Your price is used.
No EIA price yet. It is fetched when you next open directions. Your price is used until then.
Weather: alerts, radar, current weather and forecast (NWS)

National Weather Service warnings, watches and advisories for every state Southbound covers (New York to Kansas: New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware, DC, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Virginia, West Virginia and Kentucky), NOAA\'s radar as one picture of them, every airport weather station\'s current report, and the 7-day forecast for all of them (built from NWS forecasts every 6 hours and fetched from Southbound\'s own GitHub, kept on the phone). Each is one download, the same for every phone; places are looked up on the phone. Warnings on your route are shown and spoken. Nothing about you, your location or your route is sent.

Weekly average retail price for the state you pick, from the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Needs a free EIA API key (eia.gov/opendata/register.php). Nothing about you or your location is sent.
EIA has no New Jersey figure; this uses the Central Atlantic region average.

Export saves your saved places, lists, recents, Home and Work, Wi-Fi marks, API keys and preferences to one file sealed with a passphrase. Keep the file somewhere safe: anyone with the file and the passphrase has all of it. Import puts such a file back, on this phone or a new one.
Choose a passphrase of at least %1$d characters, such as five random words. It is not saved anywhere: if you forget it, the file cannot be opened.
The passphrase needs at least %1$d characters.
Exporting. This takes a few seconds.

Export failed: %1$s. The partial file was deleted.
Export failed: %1$s. Nothing was written, and the file you picked was left as it was.
When finished it will turn on these network features: %1$s.
When finished it will turn no network feature on.
Free Wi-Fi pack switched on in Settings > Maps: it downloads with the next map update.
When finished it will also switch on the free Wi-Fi pack in Settings > Maps, which downloads with the next map update.

Import replaces your saved places, lists, recents, Home and Work, Wi-Fi marks, API keys and preferences with what is in the file. It does not add to them. Export first if you want to keep what is on this phone now.

Checking and importing. This takes a few seconds.

An import was checked and kept, but has not finished being applied. Part of it may already be in place (often the saved places): Finish import puts the rest in; Discard it leaves things as they are now, part imported.
